clue.text: Englishman recalled favourite child

indicators.note: recalled in the sense of called back, so the word for the Englishman is read backwards

parts.note: POM is Australian slang for an Englishman
a favourite is a pet, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: An Englishman fondly remembers the child he liked best.
explanation.walkthrough: POM is Australian slang for an English person; 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A moppet is an affectionate word for a small youngster.

clue.text: Artist's nerve defended by partner

indicators.note: defended by means guarded on both sides, so the partner word surrounds the other

parts.note: a mate is a partner
grit means nerve, courage

explanation.surface: A painter's courage is backed up by a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Artist' stands for 'has', a link word, so the definition is just 'Artist'.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was a Belgian surrealist painter.

clue.text: Writer, one confronted by a lot of abuse, displaying neck

indicators.note: confronted by means faced by, so the earlier piece stands in front

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: abuse means insult
A means one, a single thing

explanation.surface: A writer faces a torrent of insults and shows some backbone.
explanation.walkthrough: PEN, then INSUL (insult without its last letter) facing A. Neck is a narrow strip of land, not part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A neck of land is a narrow piece jutting out into water, like a promontory.

clue.text: Relieve sly figure doffing coat

indicators.note: doffing a coat means taking off the outer layer, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, shifty character

explanation.surface: A crafty fellow takes his jacket off for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: WEASEL stripped of its first and last letters leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain is to lessen or soothe it.

clue.text: See Oscars broadcast without one winner in Best Director category

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the words are thrown into a new order

parts.note: A is one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Watch the Academy Awards on television, where one man picks up the directing prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without one' means the anagram of SEE OSCARS is made after taking out an A, leaving SEEOSCRS to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese took the Academy Award for directing for The Departed in 2007.

clue.text: Go off, as an unfortunate 21 might at work?

definitions.text: as an unfortunate 21 might at work?

explanation.surface: Someone nods off, the way a hapless racing driver comes to grief.
explanation.walkthrough: Go off means fall asleep; 21 across is Alonso, the racing driver, whose job ends early if he leaves the track in an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for falling into a heavy sleep, and also motor-racing jargon for being knocked out of a race by a smash.

clue.text: Trap in tabloid, sign giving one by 4?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a downmarket newspaper
a gin is a snare or trap for game
the Bull is Taurus, a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A tabloid snare, where a zodiac sign brings one film by 4?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts GIN inside RAG. 4 across is Scorsese, and this is one of his films; 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging Bull is a 1980 film directed by Martin Scorsese.

clue.text: Register bachelor nervously raised inside

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted up, so the letters are read from bottom to top
inside means the letters lie within the run of words

explanation.surface: A nervous single man signs up.
explanation.walkthrough: bacheLOR NErvously holds LORNE, which read upward gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up or put one's name down as a member.

clue.text: Points restricting party funds

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the outer letters hold the other piece

parts.note: E, N, W and S are compass points
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Debating points limit what a political party can spend.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points E, N and W, S enclose DO. 'funds' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow an institution is to provide it with money, so it finances it.

clue.text: Add to a fine addictive experience

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a fix is a dose of an addictive drug

explanation.surface: A good dose of something one is hooked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link here: the definition is 'Add'.
explanation.definitionFit: To affix something is to attach or append it.

clue.text: Fogy knows anger stirred one by 4

indicators.note: stirred means mixed up, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: An old fogy's temper is roused.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to 4 across, Scorsese: this is one of his films, the full title running on into 29 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangs of New York is a 2002 film directed by Martin Scorsese.

clue.text: What Sibyl did upset a rude guy mostly

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disordered, so these letters are rearranged
mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A rude man upsets someone called Sibyl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims GUY to GU; A RUDE GU is the anagram fodder. Sibyl is not a person's name here but a prophetess of the ancient world.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl foretold the future, which is to say she predicted or prophesied.

clue.text: Nationalism engulfing Scottish community

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so the word holds the answer inside it

explanation.surface: Scottish nationalism sweeps over a small island community.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in natIONAlism.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a Hebridean island off Mull, home to a famous religious community founded by St Columba.

clue.text: Drunk lad now staggering all over the place

parts.note: drunk means high, intoxicated

indicators.note: staggering means reeling unsteadily, so these letters lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunken young man reels from side to side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like part of the anagram but gives HIGH; only LAD NOW is rearranged, to AND LOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching high and low means looking everywhere, in every corner.

clue.text: Items worn by informal chap, one by 4?

indicators.note: worn by means the items are wrapped around the chap like clothing

parts.note: goods are items, articles of merchandise
fella is an informal word for a man

explanation.surface: Clothing worn by a casual bloke, one by 4?
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' casts the items as clothing wrapped round the chap. 4 across is Scorsese, and this is one of his films.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodfellas is a 1990 gangster film directed by Martin Scorsese.

clue.text: French place offering tea, we hear, tea that's not good

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its sound, so the drink gives the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: the drink's name is said exactly like the letter T

indicators.note: that's not means the following letter is taken away from the word for the tea

parts.note: oulong is a variant spelling of oolong, a Chinese tea

explanation.surface: A French town serves tea, though apparently not very good tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns the first tea into the letter T; 'that's not' removes G from OULONG, the less common spelling of oolong, leaving OULON.
explanation.definitionFit: Toulon is a naval port city on France's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Complaint made as a mogul improperly impounds book

indicators.note: impounds means seizes and locks up, so one piece encloses the other
improperly means not in the right way, so these letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A tycoon's wrongful seizure of a book provokes a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: A MOGUL rearranged gives LUMAGO, which takes B into its middle. 'made as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is a back ailment, and a complaint in the medical sense is an illness.

clue.text: A field in which there are age-old trees?

definitions.text: A field in which there are age-old trees?

parts.words: A field in which there are age-old trees?
parts.note: the field sounds like woodland with ancient trees, but it is a field of study whose trees are family trees going back generations

explanation.surface: A meadow where ancient trees grow.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of lineage and descent draws up family trees tracing ancestors.

clue.text: Cost of transport touring hot city once

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the cost word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: cartage is the charge for carrying goods by cart
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: The fare for travelling round a sweltering ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: CARTAGE goes around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was the ancient North African city destroyed by Rome in 146 BC.

clue.text: Nickname given to Ali on radio?

indicators.note: on radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: the forename given to the novelist Ali is Monica: Monica Ali wrote Brick Lane

explanation.surface: A nickname bestowed on the boxer Muhammad Ali by broadcasters.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the boxer Muhammad Ali, but the Ali here is the novelist Monica Ali.
explanation.definitionFit: A monicker, or moniker, is slang for a name, often a nickname.

clue.text: Undermine worker found with small quantity of drugs

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
a bag is slang for a small packet of an illegal drug

explanation.surface: A worker is caught with a little stash of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: To handbag is British slang, from Margaret Thatcher's style, for attacking someone forcefully in words.
explanation.definitionFit: To handbag a colleague is to savage or belittle them, cutting their standing.

clue.text: Racing driver crashing saloon

indicators.note: crashing suggests a car wrecked, so these letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A racing driver writes off his saloon car.
explanation.walkthrough: SALOON's letters rearranged give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Fernando Alonso is a Spanish Formula One world champion.

clue.text: See 26Across

annotationWithheld.why: See 26Across: second half of TAXI DRIVER, but the file has no group linking it to 26-across, so the clue's wordplay cannot be filed on either light

clue.text: Put up with facility at match

explanation.surface: Tolerating the amenities at a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate it; a stand is also the tiered seating for spectators at a sports ground.

clue.text: Latest era for renovating European properties

indicators.note: renovating means remodelling, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Developers refurbish European houses for the modern age.
explanation.walkthrough: LATEST ERA rearranged gives REALESTAT, and E for European completes it; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is land and buildings held as property.

clue.text: A Welsh hooligan with a beard

parts.note: a ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan

explanation.surface: A Welsh thug sporting facial hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The beard is the bristly tip on an ear of barley or wheat, not facial hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Awned describes a grass or cereal bearing awns, the bristles botanists call a beard.

clue.text: Vessel first sunk in channel

indicators.note: first sunk means the opening letter has gone under and is lost

parts.note: a sewer is a channel for waste water

explanation.surface: A ship goes down first in the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: SEWER loses its first letter; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug or pitcher, a container for water.

clue.text: Ordinary football side acquiring a name

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so the club's name holds the other piece

parts.note: Villa is Aston Villa, a Birmingham football club
A plus N, the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A dull football team signs someone with a reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is an English football club usually called just Villa.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is slang for plain or unadorned, the default flavour.

clue.text: See 10
Vegetables? Brand put back around plate

indicators.note: around means the reversed word is placed on either side of the other piece
put back means turned round, so the word for brand runs backwards

parts.note: to brand is to sear, mark with a hot iron
a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: Labels on vegetables are moved round a serving plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' gives RAES, which 'around' places either side of the plate word. The question mark is because radishes are one kind of vegetable, not all.
explanation.definitionFit: Radishes are pungent root crops, an example of the salad vegetables.

clue.text: Charles, perhaps, inspired by a very remote chance

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: per means a, as in two pounds per (a) head
Ray Charles was an American soul singer, so Ray is one Charles

explanation.surface: Prince Charles is moved by a faint hope.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles is not the king but Ray Charles. 'Not a prayer' means no chance, so the word alone means a slim one.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a slender hope of success is said to be having a slim possibility, 'not a ...' meaning none at all.
